proofs.proof_tex:
Assume the no-loss sequential multiscale certificate stipulated in the theorem.  Put \(D=B\wedge C\), \(p=1/(2\beta+1)\), and \(x=T^p\).  The assumed threshold gives \(L_T\le T/4\), so the certificate applies at \(L=L_T\).  For each fixed \(\pi\in\mathcal D_T\), it selects before assignment a prior \(Q_{\pi,L_T}\) supported on \(\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(B,C)\).  Hence every observed-data estimator satisfies
\[
 \sup_{Y\in\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(B,C)}
 \mathbb E_{\pi,Y}\!left[(\widehat\theta-\theta_T(Y))^2\right]
 \ge
 \mathbb E_{Q_{\pi,L_T},\pi}\!\left[(\widehat\theta-\theta_T(Y))^2\right].
\]
Taking the infimum over estimators and applying the assumed certificate yields
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\theta}\sup_Y
 \mathbb E_{\pi,Y}\!\left[(\widehat\theta-\theta_T(Y))^2\right]
 \ge
 \kappa_\beta\min\left\{\frac{B^2L_T}{T},D^2L_T^{-2\beta}\right\}.
\]
For every \(x\ge1\), \(\max\{1,\lfloor x\rfloor\}\ge x/2\) and \(\max\{1,\lfloor x\rfloor\}\le x\).  Consequently,
\[
 \frac{L_T}{T}\ge\frac12T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)},
 \qquad
 L_T^{-2\beta}\ge T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \min\left\{\frac{B^2L_T}{T},D^2L_T^{-2\beta}\right\}
 \ge\frac12\min\{B^2,D^2\}T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
The bound holds for every sequential policy, so the two infima in \(\mathrm{def{:}minimax\mbox{-}mse}\) give the claimed lower inequality.  The upper inequality is the radius-free corollary of \(\mathrm{thm{:}radius\mbox{-}aware\mbox{-}oracle\mbox{-}upper}\).  Positivity of \(B\), \(C\), and \(\kappa_\beta\), together with finiteness of \(K_+(B,C,\beta)\), gives the stated conditional \(\Theta_{B,C,\beta}\) conclusion.  This proof is conditional on the no-loss certificate; it does not establish that certificate.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(T\ge2\), \(C\ge0\), and known \(\beta>0\), the radius-aware certified window \(b_\star\) satisfies
\[
 R_T^{(2)}(\beta;B,C)
 \le
 \min\!\left\{
 4B^2,
 \min_{1\le b\le T}
 \left[
 B\sqrt{\frac{(8\mathrm e-4)b}{T}}
 +\frac{2\mathrm e C}{\beta}(b+1)^{-\beta}
 \right]^2
 \right\}.
\]
Writing
\[
 x=\left\{
 \frac{(2\mathrm e C/\beta)^2T}{(8\mathrm e-4)B^2}
 \right\}^{1/(2\beta+1)},
 \qquad z=1\vee(x\wedge T),
\]
one has the explicit scale comparison
\[
 \frac12(1+\sqrt2)^{-1/\beta}z
 \le b_\star\le(1+\sqrt2)^2z.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 b_\star\asymp_\beta
 1\vee\left(
 \left\{(C/B)^2T\right\}^{1/(2\beta+1)}\wedge T
 \right).
\]
The corresponding finite-horizon elbow bounds are as follows.  If \(x\le1\), then
\[
 R_T^{(2)}(\beta;B,C)
 \le
 \min\left\{4B^2,(8\mathrm e-4)(1+2^{-\beta})^2\frac{B^2}{T}\right\}.
\]
If \(1\le x\le T\), then
\[
 R_T^{(2)}(\beta;B,C)
 \le
 \min\left\{4B^2,
 K_{\mathrm{mid},\beta}
 B^{4\beta/(2\beta+1)}C^{2/(2\beta+1)}
 T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)}
 \right\},
\]
where
\[
 K_{\mathrm{mid},\beta}
 =(1+\sqrt2)^2(8\mathrm e-4)^{2\beta/(2\beta+1)}
 (2\mathrm e/\beta)^{2/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
If \(x\ge T\), then
\[
 R_T^{(2)}(\beta;B,C)
 \le
 \min\left\{4B^2,
 \left[B\sqrt{8\mathrm e-4}
 +\frac{2\mathrm e C}{\beta}(T+1)^{-\beta}\right]^2
 \right\}.
\]
Finally, the radius-free corollary
\[
 R_T^{(2)}(\beta;B,C)
 \le K_+(B,C,\beta)T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)}
\]
continues to hold.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(A=\sqrt{8\mathrm e-4}\), \(D=2\mathrm e/\beta\), \(a=AB/\sqrt T\), \(c=DC\), and
\[
 f(b)=a\sqrt b+c(b+1)^{-\beta},
 \qquad b\in\{1,\ldots,T\}.
\]
The constants satisfy \(a>0\) because \(B>0\) and \(T<\infty\), while \(c\ge0\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}markov\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}audit}\), for each admissible integer \(b\), the design \(\pi^{(b)}\) and the observed-data estimator \(\widehat\theta_b\) have worst-case mean squared error at most \(f(b)^2\).  The definition of \(R_T^{(2)}(\beta;B,C)\) therefore gives
\[
 R_T^{(2)}(\beta;B,C)\le\min_{1\le b\le T}f(b)^2=f(b_\star)^2,
\]
where the last equality is the definition of \(b_\star\).  This establishes the optimized Markov certificate, rather than merely evaluating it at one radius-free window.

For the second certificate, the bounded-potential-outcome assumption and the definition of the GATE give, for every \(Y\in\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(B,C)\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\theta_T(Y)|
 &\le \frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T
 \left\{|Y_t(\mathbf1_{1:t})|+|Y_t(\mathbf0_{1:t})|\right\}\\
 &\le 2B.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus the observed-data-measurable estimator that is identically zero has squared error at most \(4B^2\), under any sequential design.  Taking the infima in \(\mathrm{def{:}minimax\mbox{-}mse}\) and combining the two certificates proves the first display.

We next prove the scale assertion.  If \(c>0\), the displayed \(x\) obeys
\[
 x=(c/a)^{1/(\beta+1/2)},
 \qquad c=a x^{\beta+1/2}.
\]
If \(c=0\), set \(x=0\), consistently with its displayed definition.  Write \(M=1+\sqrt2\).

First suppose \(x\le1\).  Optimality of \(b_\star\), nonnegativity of the bias term, and evaluation at \(b=1\) imply
\[
 a\sqrt{b_\star}\le f(b_\star)\le f(1)
 =a+c2^{-\beta}\le a(1+2^{-\beta}).
\]
Consequently \(1\le b_\star\le(1+2^{-\beta})^2\le M^2\).  Because now \(z=1\), this implies the desired two-sided comparison.

Next suppose \(1<x<T\), and take \(m=\min\{T,\lceil x\rceil\}\).  Then \(m\le x+1\le2x\) and \(m+1\ge x\), so
\[
 f(m)
 \le a\sqrt{2x}+cx^{-\beta}
 =M a\sqrt x.
\]
It follows from \(a\sqrt{b_\star}\le f(b_\star)\le f(m)\) that
\[
 b_\star\le M^2x.
\]
Likewise, using the nonnegative bias summand and \(c=ax^{\beta+1/2}\),
\[
 c(b_\star+1)^{-\beta}\le M a\sqrt x
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 b_\star+1\ge M^{-1/\beta}x.
\]
Since also \(b_\star\ge1\), the last inequality implies
\[
 b_\star\ge\frac12M^{-1/\beta}x:
\]
indeed, when \(M^{-1/\beta}x\le2\) this follows from \(b_\star\ge1\), and otherwise it follows from \(b_\star\ge M^{-1/\beta}x-1\).  Here \(z=x\), proving the comparison in the intermediate regime.

Finally suppose \(x\ge T\).  Optimality and evaluation at \(b=T\) yield
\[
 c(b_\star+1)^{-\beta}
 \le f(b_\star)\le f(T)
 \le a\sqrt T+cT^{-\beta}.
\]
For \(u=x/T\ge1\), the right side equals \(a\sqrt T\{1+u^{\beta+1/2}\}\).  Therefore
\[
 (b_\star+1)^\beta
 \ge T^\beta\frac{u^{\beta+1/2}}{1+u^{\beta+1/2}}
 \ge\frac{T^\beta}{2}.
\]
Because \(M>2\), the same two-case argument used above gives
\[
 b_\star\ge\frac12M^{-1/\beta}T.
\]
The upper bound \(b_\star\le T\le M^2T\) is automatic, and now \(z=T\).  The three cases prove the explicit comparison.  Since \(x\) differs from \(\{(C/B)^2T\}^{1/(2\beta+1)}\) only by a positive factor depending on \(\beta\), the asserted \(\asymp_\beta\) relation follows.

The low-memory risk bound follows by choosing \(b=1\).  When \(x\le1\), the identity \(c=ax^{\beta+1/2}\) gives \(c\le a\), and hence
\[
 f(1)^2=(a+c2^{-\beta})^2
 \le a^2(1+2^{-\beta})^2
 =(8\mathrm e-4)(1+2^{-\beta})^2\frac{B^2}{T}.
\]
For \(1\le x\le T\), the preceding choice \(m=\min\{T,\lceil x\rceil\}\) still satisfies \(f(m)\le M a\sqrt x\).  Direct substitution gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 M^2a^2x
 &=M^2(8\mathrm e-4)^{2\beta/(2\beta+1)}
 (2\mathrm e/\beta)^{2/(2\beta+1)}\\
 &\qquad\times
 B^{4\beta/(2\beta+1)}C^{2/(2\beta+1)}
 T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)},
 \end{aligned}
\]
which is the intermediate bound.  In the high-memory regime, evaluation at \(b=T\) gives the second entry in the stated minimum, and the already proved zero-estimator argument gives its first entry.

It remains to verify the radius-free corollary.  Put \(p=1/(2\beta+1)\) and \(b_0=\lceil T^p\rceil\).  Since \(T\ge2\),
\[
 b_0\le T^p+1\le T^p(1+2^{-p}),
 \qquad
 (b_0+1)^{-\beta}\le T^{-\beta p}.
\]
Applying the optimized certificate at the admissible integer \(b_0\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_T^{(2)}(\beta;B,C)
 &\le
 \left\{
 B\sqrt{(8\mathrm e-4)(1+2^{-p})}
 +\frac{2\mathrm e C}{\beta}
 \right\}^2T^{-2\beta p}\\
 &=K_+(B,C,\beta)T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)},
 \end{aligned}
\]
as claimed.

added_lemmas.statement:
For the Markov switchback, the least certificate-minimizing integer \(b_\star\) is the pre-registrable radius-aware window.  Define
\[
 x=\left\{
 \frac{(2\mathrm e C/\beta)^2T}{(8\mathrm e-4)B^2}
 \right\}^{1/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
The low-memory regime \(x\le1\) has \(b_\star=O_\beta(1)\) and certified mean squared error \(O_\beta(B^2/T)\).  In the intermediate regime \(1<x<T\),
\[
 b_\star\asymp_\beta\{(C/B)^2T\}^{1/(2\beta+1)},
\]
and the squared exposure-standard-deviation term \(B^2b_\star/T\) and squared replacement term \(C^2(b_\star+1)^{-2\beta}\) have the same order up to constants depending only on \(\beta\).  In the high-memory regime \(x\ge T\), \(b_\star\asymp_\beta T\), while the separate zero-estimator certificate caps the minimax risk at \(4B^2\).  If one experimental period represents \(d\) units of clock time, the operational assignment window is \(db_\star\); at a mature time the retained homogeneous-history exposure comprises \(b_\star+1\) consecutive periods.  These are known-\(\beta\) oracle prescriptions and do not assert adaptation to an unknown decay index.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The exact certificate and the scale comparison are proved in \(\mathrm{thm{:}radius\mbox{-}aware\mbox{-}oracle\mbox{-}upper}\).  When \(x\le1\), that comparison gives \(b_\star\le(1+\sqrt2)^2\), and the theorem gives the displayed parametric-order upper certificate.  When \(1<x<T\), it gives \(b_\star\asymp_\beta x\).  The identity
\[
 \frac{2\mathrm e C}{\beta}
 =\frac{B\sqrt{8\mathrm e-4}}{\sqrt T}x^{\beta+1/2}
\]
then shows, after squaring, that
\[
 \frac{B^2b_\star}{T}
 \asymp_\beta C^2(b_\star+1)^{-2\beta}.
\]
When \(x\ge T\), the same theorem gives \(b_\star\asymp_\beta T\) and the independent bound \(R_T^{(2)}(\beta;B,C)\le4B^2\).

By \(\mathrm{def{:}markov\mbox{-}switchback}\), one period is one transition opportunity, so \(b_\star\) periods correspond to \(db_\star\) clock-time units.  By \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\mbox{-}ht}\), at every mature time \(t>b_\star\), the event \(H_{t,b_\star,a}=1\) retains the assignments at \(t-b_\star,\ldots,t\), which are \(b_\star+1\) consecutive periods.  For \(t\le b_\star\), the initial-boundary convention \(k_t=\min\{b_\star,t-1\}\) retains exactly the available history.  The construction uses the known value of \(\beta\) in selecting \(b_\star\), so no unknown-index adaptation statement follows.

proposed.construction:

\[
 L_T=\max\{1,\lfloor T^{1/(2\beta+1)}\rfloor\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal B_T=\{2^j:j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0},\ 2^j\le L_T\}\cup\{L_T\}.
\]

\[
 b_\star
 =\min\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{b\in\{1,\ldots,T\}}

 +\frac{2\mathrm e C}{\beta}(b+1)^{-\beta}
 \right\},
\]
where the outer minimum breaks ties toward the smallest integer.

open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen object \(\mathfrak Q_{T,L}\) is a construction handle, not an enumerated family with general-horizon transport amplitudes and likelihood bounds.  More importantly, no proved deterministic inequality relates, for every binary path, the random-offset monochromatic-block count to the sum of the arm-specific positive-part band informations over dyadic scales.  Exact cancellation of the adaptive assignment factor controls likelihood ratios once a prior is chosen, but it does not supply that occupancy--information inequality.  Intermediate mixtures of run lengths can have few monochromatic length-\(L\) blocks and non-negligible positive-part energy at several dyadic scales, so neither a single-scale dichotomy nor the formal pigeonhole principle proves the displayed Bayes-risk bound.
open_obligations.attempted: Building on the fixed-scale posterior calculation, decompose a deterministic assignment path into maximal constant runs and let \(J=\lfloor\log_2L\rfloor\).  Averaging the length-\(L\) block partition over its offset makes a run of length \(r\) contribute on the order of \((r-L)_+/L\) fully monochromatic blocks.  On the complementary run mass, attach to each dyadic \(b=2^j\) the normalized arm-specific positive-part band energy.  If one could prove that the block diagnostic plus the sum of these \(J+1\) band diagnostics is bounded below by a universal constant, policy-known averaging would select a scale before assignment and the pigeonhole bound would cost at most \(1/(J+1)\), hence \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\).  The missing premise is precisely that deterministic summed-diagnostic inequality: positive-part truncation, allocation between the two arms, and boundary periods prevent the run-mass bookkeeping currently available from proving it.  The previously enumerated path \(0000111001110101\) at \(T=16\) and \(L=4\) already rules out the naive unit-threshold single-scale version, although it does not refute a correctly normalized summed inequality.  Thus the dyadic pigeonhole step identifies the possible logarithm but does not certify it.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For a fixed length-\(L\) block prior, if \(U_L(W)\) denotes the number of blocks containing only one realized arm, the conditional posterior-variance calculation gives, up to the explicitly untreated boundary blocks,
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\theta}
 \mathbb E\left[(\widehat\theta-\theta_T(Y))^2\right]
 \ge \frac{B^2L^2}{T^2}\mathbb E[U_L(W)].
\]
For an arm-specific band alternative at a fixed dyadic scale \(b\), the endpoint displacement has order \((B\wedge C)b^{-\beta}\), while its observed-law information is controlled under the common null by the expected summed squared band score.  The assignment-kernel factors cancel under outcome adaptation as proved in \(\mathrm{lem{:}worked\mbox{-}common\mbox{-}null\mbox{-}cancellation}\).  These calculations settle constant and sufficiently long-run paths through the block obstruction and strict alternation through a zero-information band obstruction.  What remains unproved is their uniform aggregation over arbitrary concatenations of run lengths, even with a logarithmic loss.

prose_updates.tldr: The constructive side is now an exact finite-horizon radius-aware certificate: optimize the audited Markov truncated Horvitz--Thompson bound over integer windows and cap it by the zero estimator's \(4B^2\) risk.  The certified window is constant when \(C/B\) is below the \(T^{-1/2}\) elbow, has scale \(\{(C/B)^2T\}^{1/(2\beta+1)}\) in the intermediate regime, and saturates at the horizon when \(C/B\) reaches order \(T^\beta\).  The policy-uniform converse remains open: the common-null calculations do not yet prove even the proposed \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\) multiscale certificate, so the displayed matched frontier is explicitly conditional.  The \(C=0\) boundary retains the ordinary parametric frontier.

project_justification.gap: Finite-order regular-design optimization, geometric-mixing analyses, and recent sequential rerandomization do not supply a policy-uniform common-null information certificate for fixed-array polynomial memory.  The optimized Markov construction gives a radius-aware all-horizon upper certificate, but no proved deterministic occupancy--information inequality currently rules out a better outcome-adaptive policy, even with the candidate dyadic logarithmic loss.
project_justification.niche: Known beta removes adaptation to the decay index from scope and makes the candidate oracle tradeoff explicit: for the constructive nonadaptive design, exposure variance grows with the homogeneous-history window while deterministic carryover bias decays polynomially; whether outcome-adaptive assignment can beat this tradeoff is exactly the open sequential multiscale-certificate question.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution in the present core is the optimized radius-aware Markov certificate, including the trivial bounded-parameter cap and the low-, intermediate-, and high-memory elbows.  The common-null horizon-eight calculation isolates the prospective converse mechanism, while the general all-policy multiscale certificate and both its logarithmic and no-log forms remain open rather than being promoted as results.

prose_updates.related_work: Bojinov, Simchi-Levi, and Zhao analyze exact-\(m\), regular switchback designs and optimize Horvitz--Thompson risk; their result informs the constructive architecture here but is not an all-policy or arbitrary-estimator converse.  Hu and Wager study geometrically mixing Markov dynamics, whose stochastic contraction does not imply the fixed-array polynomial-memory certificate sought here.  Jia, Kallus, and Yu provide a truncated-exposure estimation template under rapid mixing and graph clustering, again informing the upper audit rather than the open converse.  Duchi and Ruan's constrained-risk inequality can be used only after close adaptive trajectory laws have been constructed and supplies no switchback occupancy inequality.  Zeng and coauthors study sequential rerandomization under no or first-order carryover.  Xiong, Chin, and Taylor inform the operational window interpretation.  Lin and Ding and Liu and Zhong address separate inference problems.  None of these comparisons is used to claim that the open all-policy multiscale certificate has been proved.
prose_updates.interpretation: For a pre-registered experiment with known \(B\), \(C\), and \(\beta\), the constructive recommendation is to minimize the displayed finite list of \(T\) audited certificates.  In the intermediate regime this means a clock-time window proportional to \(d\{(C/B)^2T\}^{1/(2\beta+1)}\); weak memory calls for a constant window, while sufficiently strong memory drives the Markov certificate to a horizon-scale window and leaves the universal \(4B^2\) cap as the safer guarantee.  Because the sequential converse is open, these prescriptions are certified upper-bound choices, not yet information-theoretically necessary windows.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The general-horizon prior family is still only a construction handle.  Fixed-scale posterior variance and adaptive assignment-factor cancellation are available, and the constant-path and strict-alternation endpoints are controlled, but arbitrary concatenations of run lengths require a new deterministic inequality coupling random-offset block occupancy to arm-specific positive-part band information.  A dyadic pigeonhole argument would lose \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\) if a summed diagnostic lower bound were available; that summed bound has not been proved.  The path \(0000111001110101\) at \(T=16\), \(L=4\) already defeats the naive unit-threshold single-scale dichotomy.  Thus neither a logarithmic lower frontier nor its no-log refinement is currently a theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The optimized Markov upper certificate, its explicit finite-horizon constants, its \(4B^2\) cap, and its radius-aware operational elbows are proved.  The all-policy common-null converse, including the proposed \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\) version with radius term \(B^2\wedge C^2L^{-2\beta}\), remains open; the no-log frontier theorem is only a conditional implication.  The no-carryover boundary is retained separately.  No unknown-\(\beta\) adaptation, confidence interval, policy-optimality certificate, or sharp leading constant is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the sole prospective root converse: it must prevent every outcome-adaptive cadence from routing around both hidden counterfactual blocks and low-information arm-specific tail bumps.
statement_notes.gap: The strengthened radius target is \(B^2\wedge C^2L^{-2\beta}\).  A dyadic decomposition suggests at most a \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\) loss, but the pathwise summed occupancy--information inequality needed to justify that loss is unproved.
statement_notes.consumer: A proved logarithmic certificate would yield an unconditional two-sided bracket with a logarithmic gap; removing the logarithm would then be a distinct open refinement.

statement_notes.justification: This audited constructive theorem minimizes the existing Markov certificate over all integer windows, adds the bounded-parameter cap, and exposes the dependence on the memory-to-outcome radius ratio.
statement_notes.gap: It is an upper certificate for one nonadaptive design and estimator, not a proof that no sequential policy can improve it.
statement_notes.consumer: Experiment owners can enumerate the finite certificate before launch and translate its minimizer into a clock-time window.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem records the mathematical implication of a no-loss sequential multiscale certificate together with the proved upper bound.
statement_notes.gap: Its lower premise is open, so the matched all-policy frontier is conditional and is not part of the proved headline.
statement_notes.consumer: If the multiscale certificate is later closed, this theorem converts it directly into the fixed-radius asymptotic frontier.

statement_notes.justification: This supporting proposition translates the exact certificate minimizer into deployment units and separates the three radius regimes.
statement_notes.gap: It is a known-\(\beta\) upper-bound prescription and makes neither an adaptation claim nor an information-theoretic necessity claim.
statement_notes.consumer: Statsig-style and marketplace switchbacks can pre-register the certified window after specifying the outcome and memory radii.
